name: Taylor Swift
description: Taylor Swift's self-titled debut launched a teenage country songwriter onto the mainstream stage and set the template for autobiographical, narrative pop-country songwriting.

name: Fearless
description: Fearless cemented Swift as a generational country-pop songwriter, sweeping the Grammys with Album of the Year and producing era-defining anthems about young love and its aftermath.

name: Speak Now
description: Speak Now was written entirely by Swift herself, framed as a series of letters and confrontations she never delivered in real life.

name: Red
description: Red marked Swift's pivot away from a strict country sound, blending arena rock, folk, and the early pop production that would define her next era.
1989 was Swift's first official pop album, a deliberate genre move built around 1980s synth production, and won her a second Album of the Year Grammy.

name: Reputation
description: Reputation was Swift's response to a years-long public feud and tabloid backlash, leaning into a darker, electronic, and percussion-heavy sound.

name: Lover
description: Lover was Swift's first album released under Republic Records and the first whose masters she owned outright, framed as a return to brighter, more romantic pop after Reputation.

name: Folklore
description: Folklore was a surprise pandemic-era release that pivoted Swift's sound into indie folk and won her a third Album of the Year Grammy.

name: Evermore
description: Evermore was released five months after Folklore as its sister record, continuing the indie-folk and alternative direction with a more autumnal palette.

name: Midnights
description: Midnights returned Swift to synth-pop production with longtime collaborator Jack Antonoff and was framed as thirteen sleepless nights across her life.

name: The Tortured Poets Department
description: The Tortured Poets Department was released alongside a surprise Anthology double-album expansion, leaning into stark monochrome visuals and confessional songwriting.

name: The Life of a Showgirl
description: The Life of a Showgirl marked Swift's reunion with Max Martin and Shellback and was framed around a burlesque-tinged showgirl visual identity.
